human_tolerance.notes: Judgement: the sources describe this as a bird of farmland, wet grassland and open pastures, with no garden-use evidence checked.

taxonomy.note: GBIF name match returned exact accepted species Vanellus vanellus, usage key 2480242, rank SPECIES (99% confidence); iNaturalist taxon 4857 is active Vanellus vanellus at species rank; checked 2026-10-31. GBIF synonyms endpoint lists Tringa vanellus Linnaeus, 1758, Vanellus cristatus Meyer and Vanellus vulgaris Bechstein as species-rank synonyms of 2480242.

external.note: Provider-specific identifiers independently resolved at GBIF and iNaturalist on 2026-10-31; both names and species ranks agree.

common_names.note: iNaturalist API preferred common name: Northern Lapwing.

range.note: GB is included as native because the ADW Geographic Range section places this migratory species throughout Europe and the account describes its British breeding and return behavior; only GB is represented here because GB is the requested activity region. Occurrence counts are not used to infer native status.

traits.body_plan.note: ADW Physical Description identifies it as a plover with wings and legs.

traits.limb_count.note: Two walking legs; wings are excluded by the schema convention.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: ADW Behavior describes ground runs and aerial attacks; mapped running to the schema Walk gait and retained powered flight.

traits.skin.note: Feathered bird; ADW Physical Description covers plumage.

traits.flight.note: ADW describes aerial diving attacks and song-flights.

traits.respiration.note: Judgement from its avian vertebrate classification.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Judgement from its avian vertebrate classification.

traits.nest_type.note: ADW Behavior identifies a ground-nesting shorebird.

traits.perching.note: ADW describes a ground-nesting, terricolous wader and no perching behavior; modeled as non-perching.

traits.size_class.note: Schema class Small because the AVONET species-level mass is 218.37 g, below 1 kg.

traits.mass_kg.note: AVONET Supplementary dataset 1, AVONET1_BirdLife row 2403, Mass = 218.37 g, n=13 individuals, Mass.Source = Dunning; converted grams to kilograms.

traits.length_m.note: ADW Physical Description, Range length: 28–31 cm. Midpoint (28+31)/2 = 29.5 cm, converted to 0.295 m; the source does not identify this as a mean.

traits.lifespan_y.note: ADW Lifespan/Longevity section labels the figure as average lifespan, status wild: 3.5 years, and attributes it to Parish et al. (2001). BTO and wildlife-trust summaries also state about four years but provide no compatible open licence or underlying locator; AnAge reports a 24.5-year wild maximum, which is not used. ADW text is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and is used as the last-resort source for this required typical-wild field.

traits.diet.note: Authored allocation 0.8 invertebrate, 0.1 seed and 0.1 vertebrate; ADW Food Habits lists worms/invertebrates, small fish and seeds/plant material, and AVONET row 2403 classifies the trophic niche as Omnivore. Percentages are model weights, not measured diet proportions. The schema uses vertebrate for fish, and small_vertebrate is the landscape resource tag used by the local behavior.

traits.social.note: Pair with size [2,2] represents the ADW Reproduction section’s solitary breeding pairs; it does not represent larger non-breeding flocks.

traits.activity_pattern.note: ADW Key Behaviors lists diurnal; Food Habits describes primarily diurnal feeding.

traits.defense.note: ADW Predation describes communal defense of nests and aerial/ground attacks; Mob is the closest schema category.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.5 for a wary, ground-nesting bird described as defending nests against predators.

habitat.note: ADW Habitat describes wet grasslands, meadows and open pasture; AVONET row 2403 classifies habitat as Wetland and lifestyle as Terrestrial. Ground/aerial split and resource weights are authored. shelter is used for open ground roosting; nest_ground is separately used for nesting.

seasonal.note: ADW Geographic Range identifies the species as migratory; Reproduction states breeding April to July. The breeding phase is scoped to GB. The regional strategy is a year-round activity simplification: the GB curve has licensed observations in all 12 months, while the share of British birds that stays for winter is not established here, so no migration fraction is asserted.

behavior.note: Species-local FSM is needed because the shared ground-forager supports only one food tag. Ground feeding uses reachable walk actions for invertebrates, seeds and small vertebrates; flee uses fly. Feeding, drinking, wandering and nest building are daylight-gated; the nest transition month set is exactly [4,5,6,7] (April through July). Rest can start when energy is high or sun elevation is below -6 degrees, and exits only after energy is low and the sun is above -6 degrees; threats can interrupt rest. Night activity is otherwise suppressed. Ground rest uses the generic shelter tag because the schema has no open-ground roost resource.

look.note: Judgement based on ADW Physical Description: dark head/breast, white flanks and belly, cinnamon undertail, green-purple wings and long crest. The block-model proportions and palette are illustrative rather than measurements.
